**Paper:** constants, theta, rho, surface classes  ·  **Source:** [fluxpy/util.py](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py)

Physical constants and the small thermodynamic helpers every other module uses.

This is the ONLY place where a physical constant is defined. The values are
those stated in the manuscript (Appendix B1: c_p = 1004 J kg-1 K-1; Appendix B3:
kappa = 0.40).

(fluxpy.util--constants)=
## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CP` | `1004.0` | J kg-1 K-1 specific heat of dry air at constant pressure (manuscript App. B1) |
| `RD` | `287.05` | J kg-1 K-1 specific gas constant of dry air |
| `G` | `9.80665` | m s-2 gravitational acceleration |
| `KAPPA` | `0.4` | von Kármán constant (manuscript App. B3) |
| `P0` | `100000.0` | Pa reference pressure of the potential temperature (1000 hPa) |
| `RD_OVER_CP` | `RD / CP` = `0.285906` | exponent of the Poisson equation, 0.2859 |
| `L137_HALF_LEVELS` | `dict` with 5 entries | ECMWF L137 hybrid coefficients (a [Pa], b) of the lowest half levels 133-137 (https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/UDOC/L137+model+level+definitions); half level 137 is the surface. |

(fluxpy.util.potential_temperature)=
### `potential_temperature`

```python
potential_temperature(T, p, p0: float = P0) -> np.ndarray
```

Dry potential temperature (Poisson equation; manuscript App. B1, Eq. B1),

$$ \theta = T \left( \frac{p_0}{p} \right)^{R_d / c_p} \quad [\mathrm{K}], $$

`T` in degC or K, `p` in hPa or Pa (see the unit helpers above).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `T` |  | required |
| `p` |  | required |
| `p0` | `float` | `P0` (= `100000.0`) |

**Returns** `np.ndarray`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L42-L49)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 42–49)
````python
def potential_temperature(T, p, p0: float = P0) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Dry potential temperature (Poisson equation; manuscript App. B1, Eq. B1),

    $$ \theta = T \left( \frac{p_0}{p} \right)^{R_d / c_p} \quad [\mathrm{K}], $$

    ``T`` in degC or K, ``p`` in hPa or Pa (see the unit helpers above).
    """
    return _to_kelvin(T) * (p0 / _to_pa(p)) ** RD_OVER_CP
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.surface_pressure_hypsometric)=
### `surface_pressure_hypsometric`

```python
surface_pressure_hypsometric(p_z, z, T_mean) -> np.ndarray
```

Surface pressure from the pressure `p_z` measured at height `z` [m] above
the surface (hypsometric equation for dry air; manuscript App. B1, Eq. B2),

$$ p_\mathrm{s} = p_z \exp\!\left( \frac{g\, z}{R_d\, \bar T} \right), $$

with the layer-mean temperature `T_mean` [degC or K]. Returned in the unit of
`p_z`. At z = 24 m and 250 K the surface pressure is about 3.3 hPa higher than
`p_z`, which lowers the surface potential temperature by about g z / c_p = 0.23 K
compared with using `p_z` itself.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `p_z` |  | required |
| `z` |  | required |
| `T_mean` |  | required |

**Returns** `np.ndarray`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L52-L63)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 52–63)
````python
def surface_pressure_hypsometric(p_z, z, T_mean) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Surface pressure from the pressure ``p_z`` measured at height ``z`` [m] above
    the surface (hypsometric equation for dry air; manuscript App. B1, Eq. B2),

    $$ p_\mathrm{s} = p_z \exp\!\left( \frac{g\, z}{R_d\, \bar T} \right), $$

    with the layer-mean temperature ``T_mean`` [degC or K]. Returned in the unit of
    ``p_z``. At z = 24 m and 250 K the surface pressure is about 3.3 hPa higher than
    ``p_z``, which lowers the surface potential temperature by about g z / c_p = 0.23 K
    compared with using ``p_z`` itself.
    """
    return np.asarray(p_z, dtype=float) * np.exp(G * np.asarray(z, dtype=float) / (RD * _to_kelvin(T_mean)))
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.era5_level_pressure)=
### `era5_level_pressure`

```python
era5_level_pressure(p_sfc, level: int) -> np.ndarray
```

Pressure [Pa] of ERA5 full model level `level` (134-137) from the surface
pressure `p_sfc` [Pa or hPa], the mean of its two bounding half levels,

$$ p_k = \tfrac12 \left[ a_{k-1/2} + a_{k+1/2} + (b_{k-1/2} + b_{k+1/2})\, p_\mathrm{s} \right]. $$

Level 136, the level of the reanalysis-driven bulk estimates, lies 3.7 hPa below
the surface pressure (31 m above the surface in the standard atmosphere).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `p_sfc` |  | required |
| `level` | `int` | required |

**Returns** `np.ndarray`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L73-L83)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 73–83)
````python
def era5_level_pressure(p_sfc, level: int) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Pressure [Pa] of ERA5 full model level ``level`` (134-137) from the surface
    pressure ``p_sfc`` [Pa or hPa], the mean of its two bounding half levels,

    $$ p_k = \tfrac12 \left[ a_{k-1/2} + a_{k+1/2} + (b_{k-1/2} + b_{k+1/2})\, p_\mathrm{s} \right]. $$

    Level 136, the level of the reanalysis-driven bulk estimates, lies 3.7 hPa below
    the surface pressure (31 m above the surface in the standard atmosphere).
    """
    (a_top, b_top), (a_bottom, b_bottom) = L137_HALF_LEVELS[level - 1], L137_HALF_LEVELS[level]
    return 0.5 * (a_top + a_bottom + (b_top + b_bottom) * _to_pa(p_sfc))
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.air_density)=
### `air_density`

```python
air_density(T, p) -> np.ndarray
```

Dry-air density from the ideal-gas law, $\rho = p / (R_d T)$ [kg m-3].

Humidity corrections are negligible for the cold, dry conditions sampled
during BACSAM-II (manuscript Sect. 3.1). `T` in degC or K, `p` in hPa or Pa.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `T` |  | required |
| `p` |  | required |

**Returns** `np.ndarray`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L86-L92)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 86–92)
````python
def air_density(T, p) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Dry-air density from the ideal-gas law, $\rho = p / (R_d T)$ [kg m-3].

    Humidity corrections are negligible for the cold, dry conditions sampled
    during BACSAM-II (manuscript Sect. 3.1). ``T`` in degC or K, ``p`` in hPa or Pa.
    """
    return _to_pa(p) / (RD * _to_kelvin(T))
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.add_theta)=
### `add_theta`

```python
add_theta(ds: xr.Dataset, T: str = "T", p: str = "p") -> xr.Dataset
```

Return a copy of `ds` with the potential temperature `theta` [K] added
(float64), computed from the temperature `T` and the static pressure `p`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `ds` | `xr.Dataset` | required |
| `T` | `str` | `"T"` |
| `p` | `str` | `"p"` |

**Returns** `xr.Dataset`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L95-L101)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 95–101)
````python
def add_theta(ds: xr.Dataset, T: str = "T", p: str = "p") -> xr.Dataset:
    """Return a copy of ``ds`` with the potential temperature ``theta`` [K] added
    (float64), computed from the temperature ``T`` and the static pressure ``p``."""
    out = ds.copy()
    theta = xr.apply_ufunc(potential_temperature, ds[T], ds[p], keep_attrs=False)
    out["theta"] = theta.assign_attrs(long_name="Potential temperature", units="K")
    return out
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.classify_surface)=
### `classify_surface`

```python
classify_surface(T_s, T_open: float = -1.8, T_thick: float = -20.0) -> np.ndarray
```

Surface class of each sample from the KT-19 surface temperature `T_s` [degC]:
`"ocean"` above `T_open`, `"thick_snow_ice"` at or below `T_thick`,
`"thin_ice"` in between (Table B1).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `T_s` |  | required |
| `T_open` | `float` | `-1.8` |
| `T_thick` | `float` | `-20.0` |

**Returns** `np.ndarray`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L106-L112)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 106–112)
````python
def classify_surface(T_s, T_open: float = -1.8, T_thick: float = -20.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Surface class of each sample from the KT-19 surface temperature ``T_s`` [degC]:
    ``"ocean"`` above ``T_open``, ``"thick_snow_ice"`` at or below ``T_thick``,
    ``"thin_ice"`` in between (Table B1)."""
    T_s = np.asarray(T_s, dtype=float)
    return np.where(T_s > T_open, "ocean",
                    np.where(T_s <= T_thick, "thick_snow_ice", "thin_ice"))
````
:::

(fluxpy.util.assign_roughness)=
### `assign_roughness`

```python
assign_roughness(
    surface_type,
    z0_ocean: float,
    z0_thin_ice: float,
    z0_thick_ice: float,
    zt_ratio: float,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
```

Momentum roughness `z0` [m] of each surface class and the scalar roughness
`zt = alpha_T * z0` (manuscript App. B2). Used when no surface fractions are
available; the paper's fluxes use the fraction-weighted blend in [`fluxpy.bulk`](fluxpy.bulk.md).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `surface_type` |  | required |
| `z0_ocean` | `float` | required |
| `z0_thin_ice` | `float` | required |
| `z0_thick_ice` | `float` | required |
| `zt_ratio` | `float` | required |

**Returns** `tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/util.py#L115-L122)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/util.py, lines 115–122)
````python
def assign_roughness(surface_type, z0_ocean: float, z0_thin_ice: float, z0_thick_ice: float,
                     zt_ratio: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Momentum roughness ``z0`` [m] of each surface class and the scalar roughness
    ``zt = alpha_T * z0`` (manuscript App. B2). Used when no surface fractions are
    available; the paper's fluxes use the fraction-weighted blend in ``fluxpy.bulk``."""
    z0 = np.where(surface_type == "ocean", z0_ocean,
                  np.where(surface_type == "thick_snow_ice", z0_thick_ice, z0_thin_ice)).astype(float)
    return z0, z0 * zt_ratio
````
:::
